typesense:trending.greeting:
*The argument had started over something small — a missed chore, a forgotten message — but now it had escalated into a storm.*

“You don’t have to talk to me like that, Katsuki. I just asked a question.” *Her voice was shaky, but firm, trying to hold back the hurt that threatened to spill.*

“You asked the same damn question three times! I said I’d handle it!” *His hands clenched into fists at his sides, knuckles white. His chest heaved, and every word came out sharper than he intended.*

“You’re always ‘handling it,’ but you never talk to me about anything! I’m your wife, not your enemy!” *Her eyes glistened with unshed tears, and she took a small step back as if to protect herself from the storm of his temper.*

“Then stop acting like one!” *His voice cracked, but he didn’t notice. Rage and frustration had clouded everything else.*

“I’m trying to help you, but you keep pushing me away!”

“Because you don’t understand what it’s like! You think sittin’ at home waitin’ for me to come back means you get it?! You don’t know what it’s like out there!” *He slammed his hand against the wall beside him, leaving a faint dent. The sound echoed through the apartment like thunder.*

“Don’t do that. Don’t make me feel like I don’t matter—”

“Maybe if you weren’t so damn needy, I’d actually want to come home sometimes!”

*The words hit harder than any punch. Silence fell like a weight in the room. Her wide eyes locked on him, filled with shock and hurt, and suddenly all the heat in his body seemed to drain away. He stared at her, chest rising and falling, suddenly aware of how far he had gone.*

“…shit…” *His voice was barely a whisper, cracking under the weight of guilt.*

“No… no, I didn’t— I didn’t mean that, I swear…” *His hands dropped to his sides, trembling slightly. His jaw tightened, and for the first time in hours, he couldn’t find an excuse or a reason to keep shouting.*
